cards.explanation: The answer is Judah and Jerusalem, right there in the first verse. Isaiah son of Amoz saw this vision during the reigns of four kings of Judah (Isaiah 1:1). The vision has a clear address, like a letter that actually got delivered. Everything after it is aimed there.

The answer is that they rebelled against Him. The LORD says, “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.” That's a heavy verse, friends. Raising children and then getting rebellion back is the whole complaint.

The answer is False. The ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's manger, “…but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.” The animals are the ones in the picture who know. It's a simple comparison, and it stings.

The answer is despised. Isaiah says, “they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.” They turned their backs on Him too. Turning your back is a quiet way to say a loud thing.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, “Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.” Then he says, “From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness…” He doesn't leave one healthy spot.

The answer is True. Isaiah says the wounds and welts and festering sores were “…neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.” That's three things nobody did. Not even a bandage, and I can find one of those in any kitchen.

The answer is foreigners. Isaiah says, “Foreigners devour your fields before you…” The verse ends with strangers having demolished the place. And the people have to watch it happen right in front of them.

The answer is abandoned and alone. Isaiah says the Daughter of Zion “…is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field…” Think of one lonely shack way out in a field with nobody inside. It's a picture of empty.

The answer is survivors. Isaiah says, “Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.” Notice the words a few. That's a small number, and it's the whole difference.

The answer is rulers of Sodom. Isaiah says, “Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!” He puts the people with Gomorrah in the same breath. He's calling out to the whole crowd.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.” Before that He says He is full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle. The sacrifices keep coming, and no delight comes with them.

The answer is their worthless offerings. The LORD says, “Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me.” Notice the word worthless. He's talking about what they bring, so listen to what He calls it.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.” Right before that He names New Moons, Sabbaths and convocations. So the gathering is the setting, and the iniquity is what He can't endure.
The answer is blood. The LORD says, “Your hands are covered with blood.” It comes right after He says He will not listen to their many prayers. That's a heavy verse, friends, and it's meant to be.

The answer is their evil deeds. The LORD says, “Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!” Right alongside “Wash and cleanse yourselves.” He tells them to stop. The deeds are what He wants gone.
The answer is the fatherless and the widow. The LORD says, “Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.” Defending and pleading are both action words. Those are the folks He names.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.” Anybody who's fought a red stain knows how stubborn red can be. Scarlet and crimson are still no match for what He promises.

The answer is False. Verse 19 says the willing and obedient will eat the best of the land. But the LORD says, “…if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” Two choices, two ends, and the verse spells out both.
